doc.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Sound before reading
summary: Rudd says he came to music through sound and dancing, with reading a later add-on; most learning came from jam sessions and recordings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah, right. I did not come from the direction of playing from written music. I came from the direction of dancing to those records while my father played, and remembering the sound, just getting off on the sound. And so pretty soon the sounds, enough sounds got into my body so that they started to build up in there in and of themselves. And so the reading, which came later, was not the primary thing for me, it became sort of an attached

facility to the actual sound. And it also became a way to get into certain kinds of music through reading. But most of my musical experience came from jam sessions and recordings — radio and later television — but mostly some kind of acoustic source that would then feed into my body and free associate and build up in there as it does.
